PullRequest.Title: Filter Agent Host slash completions by the text before the cursor
PullRequest.Body:
## Why

In an Agents window chat, putting the cursor at the start of an existing draft and typing `/pot` should offer skills such as `/pstack:poteto-mode`, and accepting one should insert it before the draft without overwriting it. Instead, the Agent Host returned no completions, and only client-side commands (`/prompts`, `/vscode-pet`) were offered.

An AHP transport log showed the request `completions { kind: userMessage, text: "/Let's rebase, …", offset: 1 }` answered with `items: []`, while the plugin providing the skill was loaded and enabled.

## What

`extractLeadingSlashToken` and `extractWhitespaceDelimitedSlashToken` took the whole run from the slash to the next whitespace as the typed prefix. With the slash typed directly before `Let's`, the prefix was `Let's`, which matches no skill or command. Both extractors now take the prefix from the slash up to the cursor. This covers every slash provider that uses them: skills (also used by Claude), Copilot commands, `/rename` and Codex `/compact`.

The replace range still ends at the end of the token. The chat input accepts with `insertMode: 'insert'`, whose insert range already ends at the cursor, so the draft after the cursor is kept. The alternate accept still replaces the whole token, for example when correcting the middle of an existing command.

The failing tests land in the first commit and the fix in the second.

## Before and after

Same draft, same cursor position, same `/pot` typed, on Code OSS builds without and with the fix.

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| ![Before: only /prompts and /vscode-pet](https://github.com/ulugbekna/screenshots/raw/main/vscode/slash-completion-before-text/before-suggestions.png) | ![After: pstack skills offered](https://github.com/ulugbekna/screenshots/raw/main/vscode/slash-completion-before-text/after-suggestions.png) |

Accepting `/pstack:poteto-mode` keeps the draft:

![After accepting /pstack:poteto-mode](https://github.com/ulugbekna/screenshots/raw/main/vscode/slash-completion-before-text/after-accepted.png)

Recordings: [before](https://github.com/ulugbekna/screenshots/raw/main/vscode/slash-completion-before-text/before.webm), [after](https://github.com/ulugbekna/screenshots/raw/main/vscode/slash-completion-before-text/after.webm).

The ordering that puts `/auto-perf-optimize` first for `/pot` is the same in an empty input, so it predates this change and is out of scope.

## How to test

1. In an Agents window chat with a plugin that provides skills, type a draft such as `Let's rebase.`
2. Move the cursor to the start of the draft and type `/` and part of a skill name.
3. The skill is offered. Accepting it inserts `/<skill> ` and keeps the draft.

## Validation

- `./scripts/test.sh --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/agentHostSkillCompletionProvider.test.ts --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/agentHostRenameCommand.test.ts` on the first commit: failed, 2 failing (both new tests returned `[]`).
- `./scripts/test.sh --reporter dot --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/agentHostSkillCompletionProvider.test.ts --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/agentHostRenameCommand.test.ts --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/copilotSlashCommandCompletionProvider.test.ts --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/copilotSlashCommand.test.ts` with the fix: passed, 179 passing.
- `./scripts/test.sh --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/codex/codexCompactCommand.test.ts`: passed, 3 passing.
- `pnpm run oxlint` on the changed files: passed.
- `pnpm run typecheck-client`: passed.
- Ran the scenario above in a Code OSS Agents window, with and without the fix.

Scenarios.Scenario: Request skill completions at a leading or whitespace-delimited slash, including insertion before existing draft text and editing inside a token, across Copilot, Claude, and Codex sessions.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Workbench completion request waits for the host's concurrent provider results. The generic skill provider resolves default-chat storage, obtains published customizations or invokes the agent fallback, optionally reads MCP metadata, then filters and maps candidates. The diff changes only the filtering prefix; token eligibility and replace-range scanning remain unchanged.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read the catalog snapshot for the one requested session when recorded default-chat storage is not already known.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Zero reads for known storage; one catalog request for the session otherwise, independently of skill count.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Exactly the same eligibility check and storage-resolution callback were executed before filtering the whole token.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The generic provider awaits storage resolution before candidate acquisition.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Acquire the session database, SELECT the mcpSkills metadata value, parse its JSON, and release the reference.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Zero if no enabled undiscovered MCP servers; otherwise one metadata SELECT per request covering all such servers, plus parsing their aggregate cached entries.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same candidate acquisition and single grouped metadata read occurred regardless of whether the old full-token prefix matched any skills.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Awaited before filtering and returning completions.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Fallback customization discovery scans workspace/user configuration and awaits plugin discovery/synchronization when the host has not published customizations.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One fallback invocation per eligible generic-provider request without a published snapshot; discovery scales with distinct roots and configuration files, not matching completion count. Copilot's command provider may separately request its fallback, as before.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Fallback ran before matching the token on both revisions, including the draft-adjacent slash scenario that returned no old matches.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Fallback completion waits for discovery; published snapshots bypass it.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Claude fallback consults supported commands, supported agents, and MCP status through its live SDK; ready Codex fallback requests skills/list and hooks/list.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Claude makes three SDK queries in parallel when a pipeline exists. Ready Codex makes two requests in parallel: skills/list groups all workspace roots in cwds, while hooks/list uses the primary root. These are absent when the published host snapshot is used.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same SDK queries and grouping happened before old full-token filtering; shortening typed does not add queries or change their scheduling.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Awaited only on the pre-existing fallback path.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Token length T, customization count C, candidate skill count S, distinct fallback workspace roots R, and discovered files F. Filtering still visits S candidates; output is bounded by matching unique slash-name/description identities, not by draft length. One metadata read serves all enabled undiscovered MCP servers.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: AgentHostCompletions uses Promise.allSettled across registered providers. The generic provider's storage lookup, fallback resolution, optional metadata read, and filtering are sequential. Claude fallback scans distinct roots concurrently and then queries its live SDK snapshot; Codex fallback is queued per session and runs discovery branches concurrently. These schedules are unchanged.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Published customizations, including an empty array, avoid agent fallback on both revisions. Known chat storage avoids catalog access; otherwise one session catalog lookup occurs. MCP cache metadata is read and parsed once per eligible request when needed, with missing or malformed data becoming empty. No cache keys, invalidation, negative-cache behavior, or retention change.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence from unchanged extractor guards and scans, candidate acquisition preceding filtering, explicit published-snapshot bypass, grouped MCP metadata access, and traced provider fallbacks.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Installed skill counts, fallback frequency, filesystem sizes, and boundary durations are not measured. No changed frequency or boundary cardinality was identified.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: prefix-only filtering restores intended suggestions. Candidate acquisition, discovery, database reads, concurrency, and retained state are unchanged. The two slices have the same bounded number of allocations and a no-longer-than-before typed substring.

Scenarios.Scenario: Offer Copilot runtime slash commands and runtime-only skills while typing or correcting a slash token.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: After unchanged customization/argument branches, the Copilot provider awaits runtime command metadata and known-skill metadata concurrently, filters command aliases, emits alias/option combinations, sorts results, and contributes to the aggregate completion response.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read the SDK runtime command catalog using rpc.commands.list through the session provider or global fallback provider.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One RPC per cold or invalidated catalog shared among in-flight callers; zero RPCs for a warm catalog. Failures may retry on later requests, unchanged.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The identical runtime metadata lookup occurred before applying full-token filtering. Changed typed text neither increases query count nor invalidates the cache.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Completion lookup waits for cached/in-flight discovery subject to the existing maximum wait; discovery can continue after timeout.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: When no published host snapshot exists, await plugin customizations, anchor resolution, pending host/client synchronization, and discovery.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Zero fallback resolutions with a published snapshot; one known-skill fallback per request otherwise, independent of runtime command matches. Generic skill provider's separate fallback is pre-existing.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Exactly the same fallback branch ran with the old full-token prefix.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Runs concurrently with runtime catalog lookup but must complete before command filtering.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Distinct runtime commands K, aliases per command, structured options, published skill count S, and completion request frequency. Output is bounded by matching command alias/option combinations after hidden-command, skill-duplicate, and alias deduplication.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Runtime catalog and known-skill lookup run in Promise.all. Simultaneous requests for the same command provider share its in-flight catalog query; warm queries issue no list RPC. Host providers remain concurrent with aggregate completion waiting for all. No new per-command or per-alias boundary calls.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: CopilotSlashCommandProvider caches successful catalogs, including empty results, and joins an in-flight list request. Completion callers wait up to 300 ms; timed-out discovery continues to populate the cache. Failure clears the in-flight/cache state for retry; invalidation isolates old requests. Published customizations bypass known-skill fallback. Plugin marketplace's separate 30-second promise cache and argument branches are unaffected by these extractors.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence from traced command-provider call order, explicit successful/in-flight cache states, list RPC callbacks, and filtering after metadata acquisition.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Catalog size, alias/option multiplicity, SDK latency, and cache-miss prevalence are unmeasured. Larger restored suggestion output is the intended behavior already supported for an ordinary slash at the input end.
Scenarios.Verdict: No high-confidence regression: only the matching prefix changes. Existing catalog acquisition, caching, alias expansion, sorting, and concurrency are preserved; unrelated marketplace argument paths do not use the changed typed value.

Scenarios.Scenario: Offer the generic /rename command and Codex /compact command before existing draft text or while editing a command.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Providers read in-memory session history/provider state, extract the token, fuzzy-match one fixed command name, and return at most one item each. They participate in the existing aggregate host response.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Token length T and completion request frequency; command inventory is fixed at one name per provider. Session history is checked through turns.length rather than a turn scan.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Both lightweight async providers are invoked concurrently with other registered providers. No sequencer, new queue, or subprocess is introduced.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No provider cache or new retained state. State-manager history and provider lookups are in-memory; cold/warm behavior is unchanged.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence from complete provider implementations and their registration callbacks, which use state-manager lookups only.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: No timings measured; the changed prefix length is at most the old token length, and results remain constant-sized.
Scenarios.Verdict: No performance finding: returning a newly matching constant-sized suggestion introduces no scaling resource cost, expensive boundary, or scheduling change.

Scenarios.Scenario: Transport and display restored slash suggestions, then accept an item without overwriting the following draft.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Workbench awaits one completion response, maps matching items, builds Monaco suggestions, and uses the existing cursor-ended insert range or token-ended replace range on acceptance. Newly available skill suggestions use the same attachment metadata and rendering path as existing slash-at-end suggestions.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Send the current draft text and cursor offset in one Agent Host completions request and receive the combined item list.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One request and aggregate response per eligible completion invocation; no per-item IPC. Payload input size remains D, while restored output size is bounded by M matching deduplicated suggestions.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same eligible token issued the same request with the whole draft and offset, even when full-token filtering returned no skills or commands.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Suggestions wait for the response; cancelled client results are discarded after the await.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Carry completion metadata in the aggregate response, map each item, and allocate Monaco suggestions.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: O(M) items after server-side skill identity and runtime alias deduplication. Prefix-before-draft output now matches the existing supported output for the same prefix without a suffix.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same mapping and suggestion path already handled ordinary matching slash requests. The changed prefix can increase results from zero to intended matches but adds no extra pass, boundary per item, richer metadata, or retention.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Mapping and suggestion construction follow the response before display.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Draft bytes D per request and matching deduplicated suggestion count M. There remains one aggregate request/response, not one IPC per suggestion. Item mapping and suggestion allocation scale with M; unchanged token scans remain bounded by token length.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Each client request awaits the host aggregate; successive typing requests may overlap because IPC cancellation is not forwarded, as before. Restored matches do not change triggers, incomplete status, cancellation, or request issuance.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No new client cache, cache key, retained attachment lifecycle, or disposal ownership. The result remains incomplete, permitting existing typing-triggered refreshes. Cancellation still drops stale returned results without forwarding cancellation over IPC.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence from unchanged client request issuance, one aggregate response, server-side deduplication, existing incomplete flag, and cursor-based insert/replace range construction.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Suggestion counts and rendering durations are not measured. No evidence establishes pathological output or a new allocation/lifecycle mechanism beyond restoring intended results.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: restored output alone is not evidence of excessive work. Full-draft transport, cancellation limitations, mapping, and insertion semantics predate the diff.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance-review pass over all three changed files and every diff page. Traced both changed extractors through every production caller, provider registration, candidate acquisition, relevant cold/warm boundary behavior, and client transport/acceptance. No high-confidence diff-introduced performance regressions found. The change fixes completion correctness rather than a demonstrated performance regression, so no regression-fix provenance was submitted. Static review; magnitude is unmeasured.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
